text: Template literals are how modern JavaScript builds strings, and they replace almost every use of plus-sign concatenation you'd otherwise write. Backticks instead of ordinary quotes, and a dollar-sign-brace syntax for inserting real values directly into the middle of the text, no string-joining gymnastics required.

A template literal uses backticks instead of single or double quotes. Anything written inside the dollar-brace is a real, live JavaScript expression that gets evaluated and inserted directly into the string — far easier to read at a glance which parts are literal text and which parts are actual data, compared to chaining a long string together with repeated plus signs.

The interpolation inside dollar-brace isn't limited to a plain variable name — any valid JavaScript expression works inside it, including arithmetic and even a full ternary expression. This gets used constantly to format blockchain values for display, like converting a raw wei amount into something a human can actually read, all in one line.

A template literal can span multiple lines directly in the source code, written exactly as it should look. A line break typed inside the backticks becomes a real line break in the resulting string, with no backslash-n escape sequences required anywhere, unlike regular quoted strings.

One term worth recognizing even if you rarely write it yourself early on: a tagged template is a template literal immediately preceded by a function name, with no space, where that function receives the literal text pieces and the interpolated values separately, before they're combined into a final string. You'll see the term 'tagged template' show up in library documentation even as a beginner.

You're ready for lesson eleven when you can write a template literal with two interpolated values, one of which is a small expression rather than a bare variable. Backticks, dollar-brace interpolation with real expressions, multi-line strings for free, and the term 'tagged template' for later. Next up: modules — splitting code across files with import and export.
